cases.reason: Half-width katakana combined with an ideographic space — the single most common shape of Japanese form input that a Western product stores unchanged.
cases.fix: Fold half-width katakana to full-width and U+3000 to U+0020 before storing or comparing.
cases.source: Unicode Standard Annex #11 / Halfwidth and Fullwidth Forms (U+FF00–U+FFEF)

cases.reason: U+30FC ー is a letter here, not a hyphen. Normalizers that fold every dash-like code point turn コーヒー into コ-ヒ-.
cases.fix: Exclude U+30FC from the hyphen set. Convert it to '-' only when it sits between two digits, which is the address and phone case.

cases.reason: Same failure in a family name: Jones written in katakana contains ー.
cases.fix: Exclude U+30FC from hyphen folding.

cases.reason: Nine distinct code points render as a hyphen. A field compared with === treats each as a different address.
cases.fix: Collapse the hyphen-like set (U+2010–U+2015, U+2212, U+FF0D, U+FE63) to U+002D.

cases.reason: U+200B is not Unicode whitespace, so trim() leaves it. The value looks identical to a clean one and compares unequal forever.
cases.fix: Strip U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060, and U+FEFF before comparison.

cases.reason: A BOM in the middle of a value. trim() removes it at the edges but not here, so the problem appears to be handled and is not.
cases.fix: Strip U+FEFF everywhere, not only at the start of a file.

cases.reason: Leading, trailing, and repeated ideographic spaces from an IME.
cases.fix: Convert U+3000 to U+0020, collapse runs, then trim.

cases.reason: A non-breaking space pasted from a web page or a Word document.
cases.fix: Include U+00A0 in the whitespace set.

cases.reason: A decomposed voiced mark. Common in text extracted from PDFs and from macOS filenames, which store NFD.
cases.fix: Compose U+3099 and U+309A onto the preceding kana, or apply NFC.

cases.reason: The semi-voiced equivalent, in hiragana.
cases.fix: Compose U+309A onto the preceding kana.

cases.reason: NFKC rewrites ㈱ to (株). That is correct for search and wrong for a stored company name, so general text normalization must not do it.
cases.fix: Use targeted width and kana folding for storage; expand ㈱ only inside a company-name–specific normalizer.

cases.reason: NFKC turns ① into the digit 1, silently changing product descriptions and notes.
cases.fix: Do not apply NFKC to free text you intend to display back to the customer.

cases.reason: NFKC expands ㌔ to キロ, changing the length and the rendering of the field.
cases.fix: Same as above: keep compatibility decomposition out of the storage path.

cases.reason: The Shift_JIS 0x8160 round-trip produces U+301C on some platforms and U+FF5E on others. NFKC folds U+FF5E to ASCII but leaves U+301C alone, so applying it makes the two diverge rather than converge.
cases.fix: Unify U+301C and U+FF5E to one code point before folding width, so both spellings of the same mark end up identical.

cases.reason: The other half of the pair: the same range written on the other platform.
cases.fix: Both spellings must produce the same stored value.

cases.expectedOutput: アメリカ・ジョーンズ
cases.reason: Half-width middle dot and half-width voiced kana in a foreign name.
cases.fix: Fold U+FF65 to U+30FB along with the rest of the half-width block.
cases.source: Unicode Standard Annex #11 / Halfwidth and Fullwidth Forms (U+FF00–U+FFEF)

cases.reason: 𠮷 (U+20BB7) is outside the Basic Multilingual Plane. Normalization must leave it intact; a MySQL utf8mb3 column truncates it and a UTF-16 loop splits it.
cases.fix: Use utf8mb4 (or an equivalent 4-byte-safe column), and iterate strings by code point ([...str]) rather than by index.

cases.reason: An Ideographic Variation Sequence on 辻 selects the two-dot shinnyou glyph. It compares unequal to a bare 辻 and is invisible in most fonts.
cases.fix: Strip U+E0100–U+E01EF and U+FE00–U+FE0F before comparing names.

cases.reason: U+FA11 﨑 is one of the twelve CJK Compatibility Ideographs that NFC does NOT fold, and it is one of the most common characters in Japanese family names. A team that applied NFC will believe this case is handled.
cases.fix: Fold the twelve unfoldable compatibility ideographs explicitly; NFC will not do it.

cases.reason: U+FA19 神 is a compatibility ideograph that NFC *does* fold — the inconsistency with U+FA11 is the trap.
cases.fix: Fold the whole U+FA00–U+FA6D block rather than relying on NFC's partial coverage.

cases.reason: 斉 and 斎 are different characters and different surnames. Folding them together merges two real customers.
cases.fix: Fold 旧字体 and itaiji only. Never fold 斉/斎 or 崎/嵜 into each other's *names*.
